newsitem.title: USA: Oregon's Senate rejects transportation tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Oregon's Senate rejects transportation tax bill.

text.p: The Oregon State Senate on Friday rejected a House of Representatives-passed transportation tax bill for the second time, effectively killing the measure for this session.

Working overtime and on the Independence Day holiday, senators turned down the tax bill, which would have gradually raised gasoline taxes by six cents by 1999 and increased vehicle registration fees. Thirteen senators voted in favor of the bill and 16 against.

Supporters, including Gov. John Kitzhaber, had strongly lobbied for the bill. Kitzhaber had indicated that he might bring lawmakers back for a special session to pass the transportation legislation, but legislative sources say that is becoming increasingly unlikely, since there is not enough support in the state Senate for higher gas taxes.
Oregon's Senate rejected an earlier version of the transportation tax bill in June.

The transportation tax bill was opposed by anti-tax activists and the state's trucking industry. Supporters argued that the measure was needed to repair and maintain Oregon's roads. The measure would have raised slightly more than $1 billion.
